title: Variance fence + reservation recalibrator and burst annealing adjustments for dedicated clusters
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: A capacity incident on 2026-03-08 exposed a class of noisy-tenant behavior where high short-lived token bursts plus poor reservation estimation caused eviction storms and degraded tail latency for co-tenants on dedicated GPU pools. Root cause analysis showed three compounding issues: (1) reservation estimator relied on mean token rates and failed to capture high-variance, skewed arrival patterns; (2) the burst policy (strict token-bucket) allowed sudden, unattenuated bursts that exhausted shared working set (KV cache pressure) and caused eviction churn; (3) noisy tenants were not surfaced by telemetry until after collateral impact had started.

Goal: Prevent recurrence by (A) detecting and isolating high-variance tenants early (Variance Fence), (B) rebuilding the reservation estimator to use percentile-weighted windows and demand-aware headroom, and (C) softening burst behavior via an annealing leaky-bucket policy + graded degradation instead of immediate hard drops.

Deliverables and non-goals: Deliverables include telemetry for noisy_neighbor_score and reservation_mismatch_ratio, a reservation recalibrator service (shadowed in prod), a new burst policy implementation with canary rollout tooling, runbook updates, and synthetic tenant tests. This ticket does not include long-term pricing/contracting changes for Dedicated customers; those will be handled by PM in a follow-up.
comments: 2026-03-10 -- Incident retro completed. Action items triaged. Agreed to pursue 'variance fence' concept (detect tenants whose coefficient of variation of per-minute token rate > 4 over a 1h window) and to implement both detection and automated soft-isolation (traffic reroute to non-eviction pool).

2026-03-11 -- Design notes: reservation recalibrator will compute weighted percentiles (p50/p95/p99) with exponential decay weights and provide headroom multiplier that varies by workload class. Proposal doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CR/Reservation+Recalibrator+Design

2026-03-12 -- Engineering sync: agreed to replace current token-bucket burst controller with 'annealing leaky-bucket' prototype. Prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/annealing-burst-proto/pull/7 (WIP).

2026-03-12 -- Telemetry task scoped: add metrics -> noisy_neighbor_score, reservation_mismatch_ratio, burst_shed_rate, kv_cache_pressure_by_tenant. Dashboard mock: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd1234/dedicated-capacity-events (shared in team).

2026-03-13 -- Quick experiment: synthetic-tenant job ran against staging; variance fence tripped for 3 of 12 tenants and soft-isolation prevented cache thrash. Logs: https://logs.redwood.ai/incident/2026-03-08/variance-experiment. Findings will be incorporated into test harness for canary rollout.

2026-03-14 -- Blocker discovered: reservation recalibrator requires cross-service access to historical per-tenant request traces older than 7d. Ops has requested retention exception; created ENG-829413 to track retention adjustment and data migration.

Build Reservation Recalibrator service: weighted-percentile estimator + headroom multiplier + shadow API (owner: Elena Kwon, due: 2026-03-24)
Prototype Annealing Leaky-Bucket burst controller, add unit and integration tests with KV cache stress harness (owner: Tariq Ahmed, due: 2026-03-20)
Add telemetry and dashboards: noisy_neighbor_score, reservation_mismatch_ratio, burst_shed_rate, kv_cache_pressure_by_tenant (owner: SRE team, owner_contact: sre-oncall@redwood.ai, due: 2026-03-16)
Create canary rollout plan for burst controller and recalibrator (shadow -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic rollback thresholds (owner: Marco Ruiz + Release Eng, due: 2026-03-26)
Update Dedicated runbook with soft-isolation steps and communication templates for affected customers (owner: Ops, due: 2026-03-22)
Add synthetic-tenant suite to CI that simulates high variance workloads and validates reservation mismatch < 20% under default load (owner: QA, due: 2026-03-19)
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for recalibrator math and burst controller; 2) Staging integration with synthetic-tenant harness (KV cache + eviction monitor); 3) Shadow run in prod for 72h capturing reservation_mismatch_ratio and kv_cache_pressure; 4) Gradual canary with automated rollback on kv_cache_pressure increase > 10% or burst_shed_rate > baseline by 2x.
rollout_plan: Shadow mode for 72 hours (no enforcement), then canary gates: 5% of tenants for 24h, evaluate metrics and customer signals, 25% for 24h, then 100% if safe. Rollback immediately on SLO regressions or >5 customer complaints. Use feature-flag flag:feat/variance-fence and flag:feat/annealing-burst.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: false positives in variance fence could penalize bursty but legitimate workloads. Mitigation: start in shadow mode and require human review before any enforced isolation; provide 'override' label for customer-exempt tenants. Risk: recalibrator unexpected under-provisioning. Mitigation: conservative headroom multiplier and slow decay of reservations; telemetry alerts and automatic rollback.
